extraction_notes.note: $g(n)=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ is introduced only inside the proof of Theorem 1 (a 3-sentence proof given no steps), yet Lemmas 1-3 state results in terms of $g(n)$; no definition node or edge carries this dependency.

The comparability graph $\widehat{G}$ is constructed inside the proof of Lemma 2 but used in the prose definitions after it and in Lemmas 3-5; left without an edge to avoid a proof-to-definition cycle.

The parser merged the \KwIn input declarations with the first pseudocode line of MULE and LARGE-MULE; kept the returned span as an initialize step. Pure \KwIn lines and \tcp comment lines of Algorithms 2 and 6 were dropped as non-operations.
Lemma 13 says 'more than $t$ vertices' while its proof argues 'size at least $t$' / 'less than $t$'; extracted verbatim.

The intuition paragraphs motivating MULE's incremental probability and maximality bookkeeping, the dataset descriptions, the input-graph table and the figures were not extracted; the intro's informal restatements of the definition and main theorem were merged into their formal nodes.

Step rule 7 requires nesting the second inline claim of Lemma 13's proof, but rules 4 and 6 (lone introduction, 'easy to see') leave a single child; kept that claim step as a leaf. Similarly 'We can verify'/'trivial' sentences in Lemmas 5 and 7 were merged into neighbouring steps.
The finishing step flags 'maximal clique' uses in Sections 4-6 without an edge from DP6; there the phrase means $\alpha$-maximal clique, so the edges come from DP9 instead (DP6 -> DP9 generalizes).
Experimental findings emitted as claims with rigor numerical rather than remarks, since they assert performance properties of MULE.

nodes.statement: First, we assume that n is even. Consider G = (V,E,p), where E = V times V. Let mboxkappa = n/2 choose 2. For each e in E, let p(e)=q where q^kappa=alpha. We have 0 <q <1 since 0< alpha <1. Let S be an arbitrary subset of V such that |S|=n/2. We can verify that S is an alpha-maximal clique since (1)~the probability that S is a clique is q^kappa=alpha and (2)~for any set S^prime supsetneq S, S^prime subseteq V, the probability that S^prime is a clique is at most q q^kappa=qalpha <alpha. We can also observe that for any subset S subseteq V, S cannot be an alpha-maximal clique if |S|< n/2 or |S|> n/2. Thus we conclude that a subset Ssubseteq V is an alpha-maximal clique iff |S|=n/2 which implies that the total number of alpha-maximal cliques in G is n choose n/2. A similar proof applies when n is odd.

$E = V \times V$. Let $\mbox{$\kappa = {{n/2} \choose 2}$}$.
For each $e \in E$, let $p(e)=q$ where $q^{\kappa}=\alpha$.
We have $0 <q <1$ since $0< \alpha <1$.
Let $S$ be an arbitrary subset of $V$ such that  $|S|=n/2$.
We can verify that $S$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique since
(1)~the probability that $S$ is a clique is $q^{\kappa}=\alpha$ and 
(2)~for any set $S^\prime \supsetneq S, S^\prime \subseteq V$,
the probability that $S^\prime$ is a clique is at most $q q^{\kappa}=q\alpha <\alpha$.

$\alpha$-maximal clique if $|S|< n/2$ or $|S|> n/2$. Thus
we conclude that a subset $S\subseteq V$ is an $\alpha$-maximal clique iff
$|S|=n/2$ which implies that the total number of $\alpha$-maximal
cliques in $\mathcal{G}$ is $n \choose {n/2}$.
A similar proof applies when $n$ is odd.

nodes.statement: Let C^alpha(G) be the collection of all alpha-maximal cliques in G. Note that by the definition of alpha-maximal cliques, any alpha-maximal clique S in G can not be a proper subset of any other alpha-maximal clique in G. Thus from Definition~, for any uncertain graph G, C^alpha(G) is a non-redundant collection. Hence, it is clear that the largest number of alpha-maximal cliques in G should be upper bounded by the size of a largest non-redundant collection of subsets of V. Let C be the collection of all subsets of V. Based on C, we construct such an undirected graph widehatG=(C,widehatE) where for any two nodes S_1 in C, S_2 in C , there is an edge connecting S_1 and S_2 iff S_1 subseteq S_2 or S_2 subseteq S_1. It can be verified that a sub-collection C^prime subseteq C is a non-redundant iff C^prime is an independent set in widehatG. In Lemma~, we show that g(n) is the size of a largest independent set of widehatG, which implies that g(n) is an upper bound for the number of alpha-maximal cliques in G.

Recall that C_ksubseteq C , 0 le k le n is the collection of subsets of V with the size of k. We have (1)~C^*= C^*_n/2 subseteq C_n/2 and (2)~|C^*| ge |C_n/2| since C^* is a largest independent set of widehatG. Thus we conclude C^*=C_n/2 which has the size of n choose (n/2) = g(n). We next consider the case when n is odd. From Lemmas~ and~, we know (n-1)/2 le L(n) le U(n) le (n+1)/2. Thus we have C^*= C^*_(n-1)/2 bigcup C^*_(n+1)/2. For notation convenience, we set n_1=(n-1)/2, n_2=(n+1)/2. Let widehatG(C_n_1, C_n_2) be the subgraph of widehatG induced by C_n_1 cup C_n_2. We can view widehatG(C_n_1, C_n_2) as a bipartite graph with two disjoint vertex sets C_n_1 and C_n_2 respectively. Observe that C^*_n_1 subseteq C_n_1 and C^*_n_2 subseteqC_n_2. Let widehatE (C^*_n_1) be the set of edges induced by C^*_n_1 in widehatG(C_n_1, C_n_2). Since C^* is an independent set of widehatG, none of the edges in widehatE (C^*_n_1) will have an end in a node of C^*_n_2, i.e, all the edges of widehatE (C^*_n_1) should have an end falling in C_n_2 setminus C^*_n_2. Note that in widehatG(C_n_1, C_n_2), all nodes have a degree of n_2. Thus we have: |widehatE (C^*_n_1)|=|C^*_n_1|*n_2 le |C_n_2 setminus C^*_n_2|*n_2= (|C_n_2|-|C^*_n_2|)*n_2 from which we obtain |C^*|=|C^*_n_1|+|C^*_n_2| le |C_n_2| = n choose n_2. Note that C_n_2 itself is an independent set of widehatG with size n choose n_2. Thus we conclude that |C^*| = n choose n_2 = g(n).
